elements.quote: Methods and Findings: All English-language published studies identi fi ed in our systematic search (up to February 3, 2021) examining the use of MSC-derived products to treat patients with COVID-19 were identi fi ed.
elements.reason: The abstract text indicates a 'systematic search' and describes the work as being based on it, but it does not explicitly identify the report as a 'systematic review' in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Three of the controlled studies reported on mortality (primary analysis) and were pooled through random-effects meta-analysis. elements.quote: Background: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) and their secreted products are a promising therapy for COVID-19 given their immunomodulatory and tissue repair capabilities. Many small studies were launched at the onset of the pandemic, and repeated meta-analysis is critical to obtain timely and suf fi cient statistical power to determine ef fi cacy.
elements.reason: The evidence states the current knowledge (MSCs/secreted products are promising; many small studies exist) but does not clearly describe “important uncertainties” beyond the need for statistical power.

elements.quote: Many small studies were launched at the onset of the pandemic, and repeated meta-analysis is critical to obtain timely and suf fi cient statistical power to determine ef fi cacy.
elements.reason: The importance/need for conducting the review is explicitly explained (repeated meta-analysis is critical for timely, sufficient power to determine efficacy).
No evidence was retrieved that cites or discusses previous similar systematic reviews or explains why a new/updated review is needed in relation to them.

elements.quote: Thus, the pleiotropic anti-in fl ammatory and regenerative effects of MSCs may point to several potential mechanisms by which MSCs exert their apparent bene fi cial effect.
elements.reason: The evidence describes hypothesised mechanisms of how MSCs may benefit COVID-19 (anti-inflammatory and regenerative effects), consistent with briefly describing a proposed mechanism of action.
There is no retrieved evidence of a logic model to show hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.
The retrieved evidence does not contain an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s) in any question-formulation framework.
The retrieved evidence does not state planned comparisons using PICO (or an appropriate variant); it only describes search methods and general meta-analysis approaches.

elements.quote: All English-language, full-text, clinical studies examining the use of MSCs or their secretome (MSC-EVs, MSC-CM) as a therapeutic intervention for COVID-19 were included. Studies could be single armed (uncontrolled) or have a comparator or control groups (controlled). For the controlled studies, all randomization methods were considered acceptable (randomized, pseudo-randomized, and nonrandomized). Studies published in languages other than English, review articles, commentaries, editorials, letters, case reports, conference abstracts, unpublished gray literature and other study types (in vitro studies, preclinical animal studies, etc. ) were excluded.
elements.reason: Included/excluded study design characteristics (clinical studies; single-arm vs controlled; acceptable randomization methods) and other eligibility characteristics (population infection, tissue sources, routes, acceptability of MSC-EVs/secretome) are specified, but eligibility details on follow-up requirements and relevant question-framework components (e.g., specific follow-up/time horizon) are not explicitly reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: All English-language, full-text, clinical studies examining the use of MSCs or their secretome (MSC-EVs, MSC-CM) as a therapeutic intervention for COVID-19 were included.
elements.reason: Report characteristics are partially specified (English-language and full-text inclusion; non-English excluded). However, the dissemination year and publication/report status (beyond full-text and types excluded) are not explicitly described in the retrieved evidence.
No retrieved evidence explains whether exclusions were distinguished as being due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported.

elements.quote: For dichotomous outcomes, risk ratios (RRs) were calculated to determine the risk of death between the control and experimental groups at study endpoint. For continuous outcomes, the standardized mean difference (SMD) between control and experimental groups was calculated using random effects meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence identifies “control” and “experimental” groups used for pooling outcomes and indicates comparisons between them. However, it does not explicitly describe the groups used in each synthesis or link these group definitions to specific comparisons defined in the review objectives.
The retrieved evidence states eligibility restrictions (e.g., English-language/full-text; exclusion of certain study types), but it does not provide rationales for notable restrictions.

elements.reason: The date when the information sources were last searched/consulted is reported as "February 3, 2021".

elements.quote: Our study has limitations worthy of mention. The number of studies and patients included in this first iteration of our review remains small. This modest number of studies and patients limits the con fi dence in the observed effects. Although this initial number of published studies identi fi ed in our search is relatively small, many registered clinical trials dealing with the use of MSC-based products as a therapeutic intervention for COVID-19 were identi fi ed in a scoping review performed by our group [31]. Additionally, only two studies reported suf fi cient information that allowed us to con fi rm that MSC products met the minimal ISCT [35] or MISEV [36] criteria for characterization. Use of MSCs that vary in terms of product characterization may in fl uence the observed effects and limit the ability to pool results from multiple studies. Signi fi cant heterogeneity was observed between studies in terms of outcome reporting. Mortality and levels of pro-in fl ammatory markers were the only outcomes reported by all nine studies included in our review. Inconsistent outcome reporting reduces the number of outcomes that can be combined in meta-analysis and limits interpretation of results. None of the studies in our review examined the use of MSCs along with other COVID-19 therapeutics. Administering MSCs along with other COVID-19 therapeutics may augment their bene fi cial effects. Potential reporting bias was also observed in all studies included in our review.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly describes limitations of the included evidence, including small number of studies/patients, insufficient reporting of ISCT/MISEV criteria, heterogeneity and inconsistent outcome reporting, absence of studies combining MSCs with other COVID-19 therapeutics, and potential reporting bias.
